provisions.title: Cleartext Transmission of Sensitive Information
provisions.text: The product transmits sensitive or security-critical data in cleartext in a communication channel that can be sniffed by unauthorized actors.

provisions.title: Sensitive Cookie in HTTPS Session Without 'Secure' Attribute
provisions.text: The Secure attribute for sensitive cookies in HTTPS sessions is not set.

provisions.title: Permissive Cross-domain Security Policy with Untrusted Domains
provisions.text: The product uses a web-client protection mechanism such as a Content Security Policy (CSP) or cross-domain policy file, but the policy includes untrusted domains with which the web client is allowed to communicate.

provisions.title: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key
provisions.text: The system's authorization functionality does not prevent one user from gaining access to another user's data or record by modifying the key value identifying the data.

provisions.title: Contact information of person to answer questions about processing
provisions.text: Every Data Fiduciary shall prominently publish on its website or app, and mention in every response to a communication for the exercise of the rights of a Data Principal under the Act, the business contact information of the Data Protection Officer, if applicable, or a person who is able to answer on behalf of the Data Fiduciary the questions of the Data Principal about the processing of her personal data.

value.reason: The Evidence is one line, `res.jsonp(response)` in routes/currentUser.ts:58. Neither the Evidence nor the data_flow (which is empty) shows what `response` holds. JSONP lets other websites read the response from another origin, so this is a real exposure if `response` includes the current user's contact details, such as an email address, as in the positive example. The file name and the 'Contact' data category point that way. But the negative example shows `jsonp` calls that only return harmless data like `{ ok: true }` or a build number. Nothing in the Evidence proves that personal data reaches this call, so it can't be confirmed as a true positive without the code that builds `response`.
